raw_response:
I farm the same 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, so I will use all 3 mu for winter wheat first, then all 3 mu for summer maize after wheat harvest. I do not like to gamble with yield. Fertilizer costs money, but if the crop comes out weak, that loss is bigger. What I do is close to what I did before, with small adjustments from what I have seen around me. For wheat, I will put the main fertilizer under the seedbed and then add one topdressing at jointing when the wheat starts pulling hard. Wheat on our side needs water at the key times, so with my well I will give it about 3 irrigations if the spring is normal. For maize, I will keep using hybrid seed because it stands better and yields more steadily than the old seed. I will put most of the fertilizer at planting and then chase one more time around the big flare stage. On only 3 mu, I count every bag, but family labor can still handle it, so I will not cut corners on seed, base fertilizer, or the main sprays. I will keep rotary tillage because it is easier for my small area and fits our wheat-maize turnover. If the weather is normal, I will aim for a steady harvest, not the very highest one.
